riskTone.label: BEARISH
riskTone.rationale: US-Iran conflict intensification is classic risk-off: dollar strength, sterling weakness signal flight to safety, bearish for FTSE 100.

orbIntel.stanceLine: Fade day — the ORB break was a trap — ORB broke UP but price has fully reclaimed the range (back below 10512.5) — the break was a liquidity sweep; the reclaim direction is in control, don't trade the original break.

orbIntel.aiStanceLine: Due to a failed upside ORB break (price reclaimed below 10512.5), 71% of the 132.8-point ADR already consumed, and UK Labour Market data printing at 07:00 BST tomorrow, any new breakout attempt today is likely to be a low-conviction trap rather than the start of a trend move.
aiBullets: Copper +1.2% makes miners bullish but the index is still -0.6% on the day — sector strength is not translating to index recovery, suggesting heavier selling elsewhere (likely large-caps like AZN or financials) is capping any bounce.

GBP sits at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range and is CROWDED_SHORT (net -72,474 contracts, improved by +17,517 w/w) — a short-squeeze in sterling would flip the GBP tailwind to a headwind for FTSE, directly undermining any long ORB trade.

With current price at 10505.6 below the ORB low of 10512.5 and only ~38 points of ADR remaining, the prior day low at 10487 is the realistic downside target — chasing shorts below there has almost no range budget support.

US futures are +0.36% (S&P) and +0.91% (Nasdaq) past the 15:00 BST mark, which historically supports FTSE into the US afternoon session — this is the one cross-market force that could temporarily halt the fade bias near ORB low support.

briefing.briefing: Sterling (GBPUSD) is down 0.3% today, sitting at a lofty 89th percentile of its 20-day range — and because UK100 and the pound move in opposite directions, that pound weakness is actually a tailwind for the index, as it makes the dollar and euro earnings of FTSE multinationals worth more when converted back to sterling. However, the index itself is down 0.6% on the day, so that currency tailwind is being swamped by other forces. The dominant regime right now is a tug-of-war: miners are the standout bright spot (copper up 1.2% is a signal that traders expect stronger global demand, lifting Rio, Glencore and Antofagasta), US markets are in positive territory (S&P 500 +0.36%, Nasdaq +0.91%), and gilt stress [a sharp sell-off in government bonds] is absent — all mildly supportive. Against that, the European tape is soft (Euro Stoxx -0.17%), the risk tone is bearish, and a Reuters headline from 16 hours ago flagged US-Iran conflict intensifying, which pushed the dollar higher and squeezed sterling — classic 'risk-off' (investors selling risky assets and buying safe havens). On positioning, speculators are heavily short the pound (a 'crowded short' means many traders have already bet on sterling falling), which is a contrarian warning that a sharp GBP bounce — and thus an index headwind — could arrive without much notice. AstraZeneca remains a wildcard: as often the single largest FTSE weight, any stock-specific news can move the whole index independently of everything else. The directional bias is cautiously BULLISH — copper strength, US market gains and the GBP sign-flip all point up — but confidence is only 5/10 because 71% of the typical daily trading range [the average distance the index travels in a day, here 132.8 points] is already consumed, the ORB (Opening Range Breakout — a trade triggered when price moves outside the first 15 minutes' high or low) broke upward but then fell back inside the range, a classic 'fakeout' or 'liquidity sweep' that now favours the downside, and tomorrow's UK Labour Market Report (07:00 BST) is a high-impact event that could trigger pre-positioning caution into the close today. The view flips bearish if AZN drops on any headline, if US futures roll over, or if sterling snaps back sharply above today's range. For the 08:00 ORB trade specifically, today is a fade-favoured, stand-aside-or-short-bias day: the upside break already failed, 71% of range is used, and event risk tomorrow argues against chasing fresh breakouts. Key levels: overnight high 10577.1 and ORB high 10559.2 are resistance; ORB low / overnight low 10512.5 is the line in the sand — a confirmed hold below there keeps the short bias alive; prior day low 10487 is the next meaningful target if sellers press. With only ~38 points of typical daily range left (29% of 132.8 ADR), new positions need tight targets. Tomorrow, the UK Labour Market Report at 07:00 BST prints one hour before the cash open — position sizing should be reduced ahead of that release, and Wednesday's UK CPI (07:00 BST) piles on further event risk later this week.
